title: Jalapeño's First Results
hook: OpenAI's custom inference chip, co-designed with Broadcom, now has numbers attached — the lab claims industry-leading speed and efficiency on modern models.
key_points: Jalapeño is OpenAI's custom chip built specifically for inference rather than training.
This post reports its first results: faster and more power-efficient inference than the alternatives OpenAI compares against.
The claimed wins are higher throughput and lower latency on modern models.
It continues the pattern of frontier labs designing their own silicon rather than buying general-purpose GPUs.
content_html: OpenAI has published the first performance results for Jalapeño, the inference chip it co-designed with Broadcom. The lab describes faster and more power-efficient inference than its comparison points, with higher throughput and lower latency on current models.
extra_html:
Reading the claim

These are first-party numbers from a company with an obvious interest in the outcome, and the post is a launch update rather than an independent benchmark — so the headline framing deserves the usual discount until third parties measure it. What is not in doubt is the strategic direction. Specializing a chip to inference lets you drop everything a training accelerator needs and spend the area and power on serving tokens instead, which is where the recurring cost of a deployed model actually lives. Google went this way with the TPU and Microsoft with Maia; Jalapeño is OpenAI taking the same step for its own workload.

flashcards.back_html: Inference — serving already-trained models — rather than training, which is what lets it target better throughput, latency, and power than a general-purpose GPU.
